table.title: EN · Long headers, short data
table.md:
| Region | Quarterly revenue (USD, millions) | Year-over-year growth rate | Number of active enterprise customers | Net promoter score |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| NA | 412.5 | 12% | 1,204 | 61 |
| EMEA | 287.1 | 9% | 986 | 58 |
| APAC | 198.4 | 21% | 640 | 64 |
| LATAM | 54.0 | 17% | 133 | 55 |

understanding.purpose: Compare regional revenue, growth, enterprise customer counts, and customer sentiment.
understanding.reading: Readers scan across each region to relate its measures, and down each metric to compare regions. The long headers can occupy several lines while the short data rows remain compact.
groups: Region identifies each row; its labels anchor comparisons across all four measures.
Revenue and year-over-year growth describe financial performance.
Enterprise customer count and net promoter score describe the customer base and its sentiment.
keep_intact: Numeric values, percentages, and other individual data values
Individual words and the USD currency identifier
may_wrap: Long headers at natural word boundaries, including the revenue unit in parentheses
The shorter Region header should remain on one line

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Give net promoter the 161px needed for its full header on one line, taking space mainly from the region and enterprise columns. This tests whether a shorter final heading improves the overall rhythm while keeping the other long headings readable.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Refine r0A with a little more room for Region and revenue, taking space from customer count while preserving the two-line header rhythm.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Refine r0B by shifting a little space from revenue to customer count, while retaining emphasis on the financial measures.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Try a more even distribution across the four measures, giving sentiment more breathing room while reserving extra width for the longest customer header.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Refine r1A by narrowing the region column and giving the recovered space to net promoter. Retain the generous enterprise width and the established two-line header pattern, while giving the last heading more breathing room.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Start from r2A and move 10px from growth to customer count. This gives the longest header more room while preserving the one-line net promoter score header; check that growth still wraps cleanly into two lines.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Give customer count more space by narrowing both financial columns. This tests a more pronounced allocation to the longest header while retaining the one-line net promoter score; check the revenue and growth breaks for balance.

bad.name: r0C
bad.note: Prioritize the exceptionally long enterprise-customer header and accept deeper wrapping in the other metric headers.
bad.why: The customer column is disproportionately wide for its short values, while the revenue and promoter-score headers each need three lines. This produces an uneven header and wastes space that would help neighboring columns.

rationale: r2A gives the region labels enough room and distributes the remaining width among the four measures without making the customer column dominate. Its three longer headers fit on two lines, while Net promoter score stays on one line; the short numeric values remain easy to scan down their columns. The ranges are approximate visual tolerances, with the other columns adjusted proportionally to stay within the width limit.

general: Allocate width to the needs of both headers and data, rather than making columns equal by default.
Keep words intact and preserve recognizable phrases when headers wrap.
Judge the rhythm of the whole table as well as individual column widths.
specific: The short region labels need relatively little width.
The measure headers drive the width allocation because their values are short.
Giving the promoter-score header enough room for one line works here without forcing the other headers beyond two lines.

tradeoffs: r3A and r3B give the customer header more breathing room, but narrow the growth or revenue columns. The r1 designs retain a wider region column at the cost of wrapping the promoter-score header.
uncertain: Designers could reasonably prefer a more uniform two-line treatment for all measure headers, or more space around the customer header. The stated ranges are estimates from the supplied renders, not independently rendered breakpoints.

critique.good: The four measures have balanced two-line headers, and the compact rows make regional comparisons easy. Revenue keeps its unit together, and all data values remain intact.
critique.problems: The customer-count column has noticeably more open space than the other measures, while Region is comparatively tight.
critique.cause: The 205px customer-count column is wider than needed for its two header lines; Region has only 75px.

critique.good: The 80px Region column gives the row labels comfortable space. The two-line metric headers and compact rows create a consistent rhythm, with revenue and growth given useful emphasis.
critique.problems: The customer-count header is relatively crowded, while the revenue column has spare space. The sentiment column is also a little tighter than its peers.
critique.cause: Revenue gets 180px, while the longer customer-count header gets the same width and sentiment gets 129px.

critique.good: The customer-count header has ample room, and the region labels and data values remain intact.
critique.problems: Revenue and sentiment wrap to three lines, creating a taller header and an uneven distribution of white space. The very wide customer-count column separates its values from the financial measures.
critique.cause: The 260px customer-count column takes space from revenue at 140px and sentiment at 99px.

critique.good: The region labels and numeric values remain intact, and the compact data rows make both cross-region and within-region comparisons easy. All four measure headers wrap at natural boundaries into two lines.
critique.problems: The last header leaves “score” alone on its second line, while the enterprise column has comparatively generous white space.
critique.cause: The 134px net promoter column is too narrow for the full header; the 195px enterprise column has room that could be redistributed.

critique.good: The two-line revenue and enterprise headers read clearly, and the compact rows preserve a steady scanning rhythm.
critique.problems: The extra width given to revenue does not visibly improve its line break. “Score” still sits alone, and the enterprise header has less breathing room than in r1A.
critique.cause: Revenue grows to 175px without reaching a useful new wrapping threshold, while net promoter narrows to 129px and enterprise to 185px.

critique.good: The headers retain coherent word groups, and the enterprise column has enough room for a balanced two-line heading. The data remain easy to compare.
critique.problems: The last header still ends with an isolated “score.” The small redistribution from r1A does not produce a meaningful improvement in the visible header hierarchy.
critique.cause: At 139px, net promoter remains below the width needed for its complete header on one line; revenue is reduced to 160px without changing its visible wrap.

critique.good: Region labels and all values remain intact. The short data rows read clearly across, while the right-aligned measures support comparison down each column. Revenue, growth, and customer count each use two header lines; net promoter score fits on one.
critique.problems: The customer-count header feels slightly crowded compared with the space around the shorter net promoter score header. The financial headers also have a somewhat uneven distribution of space.
critique.cause: The customer-count column has 160px of text width, while the net promoter score column has 140px, just enough for its entire header. The growth column has some space that could potentially be reassigned.

critique.good: The wider customer-count column gives its long header more breathing room. Region labels and values remain intact, and the two-line headers establish a consistent header height.
critique.problems: The net promoter score header breaks before “score,” leaving a short second line. This makes the last column feel cramped even though its data values are very short.
critique.cause: Reducing the last column to 142px leaves only 121px for text, below the header’s 140px one-line width. The extra width goes mainly to the customer-count column, whose header already fits in two lines in r2A.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0C.why: The values are intact and easy to scan, but the very wide customer column and narrow score column produce uneven spacing and three-line headers.

ref_auto.why: All headers fit naturally in two lines, with a compact region column and generous space for the longer customer heading. Rows and numeric columns scan cleanly.

r1B.why: The two-line headers and well-proportioned columns give the table a steady rhythm, while keeping the region labels compact and the figures easy to compare.

r1A.why: The headers wrap cleanly to two lines and the data is easy to scan. The score column is somewhat generous relative to its short values.

r2A.why: The table is legible and the first four columns are compact, though the wider score column leaves noticeably more space around its short values.

ref_equal.why: The data remains clear, but the wide region column leaves substantial unused space and the revenue and customer headings need three lines.

raw.unsure: B and C are very close; their small differences in column proportions make the choice between them largely a matter of judgment.

ref_equal.why: The columns have a steady rhythm, but the region column is unnecessarily wide and the revenue and customer headers each need three lines.

r0C.why: All content fits, but the customer column has conspicuously more space than its short values need, while two other headers wrap to three lines.

r2A.why: The narrow region column leaves room for balanced metric columns; the headers wrap cleanly in at most two lines, and rows scan easily.

ref_auto.why: Headers wrap cleanly and rows read well, though the customer column feels somewhat wide for its values and the score column is relatively tight.

r1B.why: The metric columns are well proportioned and headers wrap cleanly, although the region column has a little more space than it needs.

r1A.why: The headers and data are clear, with a consistent two-line header rhythm; the region column is slightly generous for its short labels.

raw.unsure: C, D, E and F are close; the preference among them depends on how much weight to give the single-line score header versus a more consistent two-line header rhythm.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
